results.title: Denominator of a rational polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a polynomial $P \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$, the denominator $\operatorname{denom}(P)$ is the least common multiple of the denominators (in lowest terms) of the nonzero coefficients of $P$; in particular $\operatorname{denom}(0) = 1$. Thus $\operatorname{denom}(P) = 1$ exactly when $P \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$.

results.title: Coefficient denominators divide the denominator of a polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every polynomial $P \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the denominator (in lowest terms) of the coefficient of $x^i$ in $P$ divides the denominator $\operatorname{denom}(P)$ of $P$.

results.title: Denominator one characterizes integer polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every polynomial $P \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$, its denominator $\operatorname{denom}(P)$ equals $1$ if and only if, for every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the coefficient of $x^i$ in $P$ is an integer.

results.title: Real-rooted polynomials
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A complex polynomial $p$ is real-rooted if every element $z$ of its multiset of roots is real, that is, $\operatorname{Im} z = 0$.

results.title: Conjugation-invariant polynomials with roots in the closed lower half-plane are real-rooted
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a nonzero complex polynomial that is unchanged when complex conjugation is applied to each of its coefficients. If every root $z$ of $p$ satisfies $\operatorname{Im} z \le 0$, then $p$ is real-rooted.

results.title: Largest real part of a root
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a complex polynomial $p$, let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part $\operatorname{Re} z$ of an element $z$ of the multiset of roots of $p$, with $\rho(p) = 0$ when that multiset is empty (as it is for nonzero constants and for $p = 0$).

results.title: Real parts of roots are bounded by the largest one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a complex polynomial and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of an element of its multiset of roots, or $0$ if that multiset is empty. Then every element $z$ of the multiset of roots of $p$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re} z \le \rho(p)$.

results.title: The largest real part of a root is attained
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a complex polynomial whose multiset of roots is nonempty, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of a root of $p$. Then some root $z$ of $p$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re} z = \rho(p)$.

results.title: Nonconstant complex polynomials have a root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every complex polynomial of positive degree has at least one root.

results.title: For a real-rooted polynomial, the largest real part of a root is a root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a real-rooted complex polynomial of positive degree, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of a root of $p$. Then the real number $\rho(p)$, viewed as a complex number, is a root of $p$.

results.title: Monic real-rooted polynomials have positive real part right of the largest root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a monic real-rooted complex polynomial, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of a root of $p$, or $0$ if $p$ has no roots. Then $\operatorname{Re} p(x) > 0$ for every real number $x > \rho(p)$.

results.title: Monic real-rooted polynomials have nonnegative real part from the largest root on
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a monic real-rooted complex polynomial, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of a root of $p$, or $0$ if $p$ has no roots. Then $\operatorname{Re} p(x) \ge 0$ for every real number $x \ge \rho(p)$.

results.title: Maximal residue-class error

results.title: Maximal residue-class error up to a level

results.title: Prime-power bound for primitive non-deficient numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\sigma(m)$ denote the sum of the divisors of $m$. Let $n$ be a positive integer that is non-deficient, $\sigma(n) \ge 2n$, and primitive, meaning that every divisor $m$ of $n$ with $m < n$ is deficient, $\sigma(m) < 2m$. Let $k$ be the number of distinct prime factors of $n$ and $R$ their product. Then $n$ has a prime factor $p$ with $p^{v_p(n) + 1} < 2kR$, where $v_p(n)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $n$.

results.title: Non-deficient number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is non-deficient when $n \ne 0$ and $\sigma(n) \ge 2n$, where $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of the positive divisors of $n$.

results.title: Primitive non-deficient number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is primitive non-deficient when it is non-deficient and every proper divisor $m$ of $n$ (a divisor with $m < n$) is deficient, that is, $\sigma(m) < 2m$, where $\sigma(m)$ is the sum of the positive divisors of $m$.

results.title: Abundancy index
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the abundancy index is the rational number $h(n) = \sigma(n)/n$, where $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of the positive divisors of $n$.

results.title: Product of $p/(p-1)$ over the prime factors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $H(n) = \prod_p p/(p-1)$ in $\mathbb{Q}$, the product over the distinct primes $p$ dividing $n$. For $n = 0$ the product is empty ($0$ is taken to have no prime factors), so $H(0) = 1$.

results.title: Odd numbers with two prime factors are deficient

results.title: Grün's bound for non-deficient numbers

results.title: The ideal of a form is nonzero

results.title: Ideal class of a binary quadratic form

results.title: Unit strip

results.summary: The unit strip is the set of points $(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with $0 \le x \le 1$, that is, $[0, 1] \times \mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Gluing map of the Moebius band
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $a$, this is the map $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ given by $(x, y) \mapsto (1 - x, y + a)$.

results.title: Fundamental domain of the Moebius band
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $a$, this is the set of points $(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with $0 \le x \le 1$ and $0 \le y < a$.

results.title: Moebius embedding
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $a$ be a real number, let $S = [0, 1] \times \mathbb{R}$ be the unit strip and let $f : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3$. Then $f$ is a Moebius embedding of aspect ratio $a$ if $f(1 - x, y + a) = f(x, y)$ for every $(x, y) \in S$, $f$ is $C^\infty$ on $S$, at every point of $S$ the derivative of $f$ within $S$ is a linear isometry $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3$, and $f$ is injective on $[0, 1] \times [0, a)$.

results.title: Schwartz's optimal paper Moebius band theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a > 0$. If $f : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ is a Moebius embedding of aspect ratio $a$, then $a > \sqrt{3}$. That is, a smooth embedded paper Moebius band has aspect ratio greater than $\sqrt{3}$.

results.title: First passage of the exploration walk
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The exploration walk started at `k` with steps `x_i - 1` stays positive at every time `j < n`: `j < k + ∑_{i < j} x_i`. Together with `∑ x_i + k = n` this says that the walk first hits `0` at time `n`.

results.title: Cyclic shift of a tuple
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The cyclic shift `i ↦ x_{(i + r) mod n}` of a tuple.

results.title: Cycle lemma
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Cycle lemma (Dvoretzky–Motzkin 1947). If `x : Fin n → ℕ` satisfies `∑ x_i + k = n` with `1 ≤ k`, then exactly `k` of the `n` cyclic shifts of `x` (counted by shift `r < n`) are first-passage sequences.

results.title: Walk weight of step sequences ending at zero
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The weight `W_p(k, n) = ∑ ∏_i p(x_i)` over the step sequences `x : Fin n → ℕ` with `∑ x_i + k = n` (the walk from `k` is at `0` at time `n`). For `p(j) = P(ξ = j)` this is `P(ξ_1 + ⋯ + ξ_n = n - k)` when `k ≤ n`, and `0` when `k > n`.

results.title: Hitting weight of first-passage step sequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The weight `H_p(k, n) = ∑ ∏_i p(x_i)` over the step sequences with `∑ x_i + k = n` along which the walk from `k` first hits `0` at time `n`. For `p(j) = P(ξ = j)` this is the probability `P(T = n)` that the total progeny of `k` ancestors is `n`.

results.title: Hitting-time theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Hitting-time theorem, weighted form: `n · H_p(k, n) = k · W_p(k, n)` for every weight `p` with values in a commutative semiring and all `k, n`. For probability weights this is the hitting-time theorem of van der Hofstad–Keane (2008); the proof double counts cyclic shifts with the cycle lemma.

results.title: Probability of first passage at time n
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under `ν^{⊗n}`, the event that the walk from `k` first hits `0` at time `n` has measure `H_p(k, n)` with `p(j) = ν{j}`. When `ν` is a probability measure this is the probability `P(T = n)`.

results.title: Probability of the offspring walk event as a walk weight
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under `ν^{⊗n}`, the event `ξ_1 + ⋯ + ξ_n + k = n` has measure `W_p(k, n)` with `p(j) = ν{j}`. When `ν` is a probability measure this is the probability `P(ξ_1 + ⋯ + ξ_n = n - k)`.

results.title: Otter–Dwass formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For i.i.d. offspring numbers with law `ν` and `k` ancestors, the finite-measure identity `n · P(T = n) = k · P(ξ_1 + ⋯ + ξ_n = n - k)` holds as an identity of event masses (Otter 1949; Dwass 1969); the two sides are probabilities when `ν` is a probability measure.

results.title: Walk weights for Poisson offspring
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For Poisson(`r`) step weights, `W_p(k, n) = e^{-rn} (rn)^{n-k} / (n-k)!` when `k ≤ n`: the sum of `n` independent Poisson(`r`) variables is Poisson(`rn`).

results.title: Borel–Tanner law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For Poisson(`r`) offspring and `k ≤ n` ancestors, `n · P(T = n) = k e^{-rn} (rn)^{n-k} / (n-k)!` (Tanner 1961; Haight–Breuer 1960).

results.title: Borel law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For Poisson(`r`) offspring and one ancestor, the total progeny satisfies `P(T = n) = e^{-rn} (rn)^{n-1} / n!` for `n ≥ 1` (Borel 1942).

results.title: Graphs with the same chromatic symmetric function
